comparator.name: Nederlands, Europees en Internationaal Recht
comparator.sourceNotes: Adopted annual OER, effective 1 September 2026, Appendix VI Article 2 pp53–55: 60 EC in each year, 180 EC total. Regular full-time pathway, with Philosophy of Law selected from the required 4-EC metajuridical choice; 176 compulsory EC plus 4 restricted-choice EC, no open elective space or regular internship. OER retains European Law School and code50017. The current name is expressly bridged by the main programme page and university registration regulation, adopted21 September2026, PDFp44: Nederlands, Europees en Internationaal recht50017. Main-page factsheet57085 conflicts; do not substitute it for controlling identity. No hidden/visible edition conflict: visually inspected OERpp3,54–56 and registrationp44. B1 noncredit Tutoraat participation required. General Article8: B1 completion, or at least45EC plus subject-specific prerequisites, for B2/B3; AppendixVI lists exact prerequisites. Thesis5EC requires Academic Language Skills and Academic SkillsI/II; transitionp3 permits previously passed Foutloos Nederlands instead of new language unit, not relevant to selected new entrants. Thesis regulation:4000–5000 words, approximately3months, mandatory group meetings. B1 active/prepared workgroup participation gates examinations; ordinary BSA45EC. Separate French–Dutch translation route replaces10EC of B2 study and requires diagnostic French preparation0EC; not mixed into the regular route. No RADAr requirement identified in these controlling law documents.

alternatives.label: Law, European institutions and international justice
alternatives.concept: Study constitutional, criminal, private, European Union, human-rights and public international law, with transnational business law and sustained analysis of political institutions, society and public argument. The legal courses provide a substantive response to the programme’s European and international focus. Dutch civil and procedural depth, specialised legal-research training, assessed moot courts and the required legal thesis remain substantial gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual enriched content establishes60EC of legal study:52.5EC across the law foundation and sixLAWJ courses plus7.5EC transnational business law. Politics, sociology, ethics, governance, history and communication provide identified complements; they are not counted as additional doctrinal law. The programme has a sustained legal core, not only adjacent coherence. It does not constitute the Dutch professional legal pathway.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes all formally dependent 200/300-level law courses; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law. Comparative politics and sociology foundations precede advanced EU politics and social theory, and all course offerings and formal prerequisites are satisfied.

candidates.label: French–Dutch legal translation
candidates.reason: The separate specialist route requires French language proficiency and translation of legal texts. The UCR workbook offers no French language or French–Dutch legal translation sequence; general stylistics and Dutch cannot sustain a distinct 24-course translation curriculum.

candidates.label: European and international legal advocacy
candidates.reason: The strongest available UCR legal, EU, international and rhetoric courses already anchor the closest-match programme. A second advocacy label would retain that core and reshuffle complementary courses without changing its academic priority or producing a substantively different legal curriculum.

routeSelection.basis: Exact programme registry50017 European Law School, now Nederlands, Europees en Internationaal Recht. Current adopted annual OER establishes a complete regular pathway for new2026 entrants without legacy credit substitutions or translator route mixing.

selection.assessment: One 24-course law-led response captures the Dutch, EU and international law core with explicitly limited Dutch procedural and civil-law depth. The French–Dutch translation specialisation is not feasible with the current UCR course offer; legal advocacy is already substantively integrated into the first alternative and cannot justify a distinct second curriculum.

notes.text: Radboud requires sustained Dutch civil and procedural law, specialist legal research, moot courts and a 5-EC legal thesis. The UCR programme offers substantive law with wider political and social study, but does not reproduce these requirements or confer Dutch professional legal qualification.

audience.programmeDescription: Nederlands, Europees en Internationaal Recht, formerly European Law School, combines Dutch law with European Union and international law. This comparison follows the regular full-time pathway in the adopted 2026–2027 regulations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programme includes constitutional, criminal, private, EU, human-rights, international and transnational business law. Political institutions, social research, ethics and communication add context. It offers substantial legal study, while Radboud’s Dutch civil and procedural sequence, specialist legal research, assessed moot courts and required legal thesis remain gaps. General rhetoric, qualitative methods and stylistics do not replace legal training.

curriculum.limitation: Each year contains 60 EC. The programme requires 176 EC of compulsory study plus one 4-EC restricted metajuridical choice, shown here as Philosophy of Law. There is no open elective space. Noncredit first-year Tutoraat participation and active, prepared participation are additional requirements. The ordinary first-year study-advice threshold is 45 EC.

componentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 5-EC legal thesis, 4000–5000 words. Entry requires Academic Language Skills and Academic Skills I and II; mandatory group meetings apply.
componentNotes.y3-choice: Choose one 4-EC metajuridical subject: European legal history, sociology of law or philosophy of law. This example selects philosophy of law.
